solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Partially rebuff a lonely creature

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer sits inside a run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of rebuff, the a and the start of lonely

explanation.surface: A solitary animal is given a half-hearted snub.
explanation.definitionFit: The buffalo is a large wild ox, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Snake and wild pig with no tail

indicators.note: an animal without its tail has lost its back end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: Two wild creatures, one of them maimed, seen together in the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a large constricting snake of the Americas, so the word is a direct hyponym.

clue.text: Confront carrying water heater — it's very hot!

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: to face something is to confront it
an urn is a large vessel for heating water, as for tea

explanation.surface: Someone tackling a scalding boiler is warned it is very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water heater' looks like the definition, but it supplies the urn; the definition is the exclamation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace is an enclosed chamber burning at intense temperatures, the proverbial very hot place.

clue.text: Bypass article on vacuum

blocks.note: a void is an empty space, a vacuum

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about vacuum cleaners gets skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the article sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go around it, i.e. to steer clear of it.

clue.text: Unfashionable to support Australia, mostly?

blocks.note: out of fashion, no longer in
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Supporting the Australian team is not the trendy thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description: most of Australia's land area is remote interior.
explanation.definitionFit: The outback is the vast, thinly populated hinterland that makes up most of the Australian continent.

clue.text: What's owed during every big transfer, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Money owed on each large football transfer deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum of money owed by one party to another.

clue.text: Wine served up by English city

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A wine poured out by a local of some English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby is a city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Courageous to ring in with a fantastic idea

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the first word goes around the next ones

blocks.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: It takes courage to phone in with a great suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring in' reads as phoning a radio show; 'ring' is the container signal, and 'in', 'with' and 'a' all go inside the courageous word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden inspired thought, a brilliant idea.

clue.text: Mohican, perhaps, hid oar clumsily

indicators.note: something done clumsily is botched, so the letters fall out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Mohican warrior awkwardly conceals a canoe paddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mohican suggests the Native American people, but here it is the spiky haircut named after them (a mohawk).
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a style of haircut, so it is an example of a hairdo, as 'perhaps' warns.

clue.text: Paintings, say, framed by light-brown material

indicators.note: something framed by another thing has that thing all around its edges

blocks.note: tan is a light brown colour
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: Pictures mounted in light brown fabric frames.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is a woollen cloth woven in a checked pattern, a kind of material.

clue.text: £1,000 swindle snaring an unknown US attraction

indicators.note: a trap snaring prey holds it inside, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns

explanation.surface: A thousand-pound scam traps an unsuspecting American tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: The swindle goes around 'an' plus the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is one of America's most visited natural sights, a tourist attraction.

clue.text: Gold tiara fashioned for competitor in arena

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters are remade into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A golden crown made as the prize for a champion of the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator fought other combatants or beasts in the Roman arena, so he competed there.

clue.text: Look — boy cut down garden structure

indicators.note: a thing cut down is shortened, losing its final letter

blocks.note: to gaze is to look steadily

explanation.surface: Someone points out a lad felling a summerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small roofed pavilion in a garden, open at the sides.

clue.text: Host regularly greeting Shakespeare character

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: A host routinely welcomes a guest dressed as a Shakespeare figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moorish general who is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Snatch baby goat before short rest

blocks.note: a kid is a young goat
a nap is a brief sleep

explanation.surface: Grab the young goat before it has a quick snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to seize and carry someone off, i.e. to snatch them.

clue.text: Protection from extremely destructive barrier

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its two ends

explanation.surface: A fence that shields you from something very damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely destructive' reads as 'very destructive', but it means just the outside letters of destructive.
explanation.definitionFit: Defence means shielding or guarding against attack, a synonym for protection.

clue.text: Officer, he is mixing alcoholic drink!

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman caught making cocktails on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish coffee is hot coffee laced with Irish whiskey and topped with cream, a spirit-based drink.

clue.text: Press ultimately employ sarcasm

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Journalists end up resorting to sneering mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests newspapers, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony and sarcasm both say the opposite of what is meant; the clue treats them as loose synonyms.

clue.text: Nothing unchanged for rock band

blocks.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
as is means left in its present state

explanation.surface: No alterations made for a touring rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis were the Manchester rock band led by the Gallagher brothers, famous in the 1990s Britpop era.

clue.text: Wander with small fairy-tale villain

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a troll is the menacing creature under the bridge in fairy tales

explanation.surface: Roaming about in the company of a little storybook baddie.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk in a leisurely aimless way, which is to wander.

clue.text: Cook used an ice cream

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef made use of an ice cream in a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundae is a dessert of ice cream topped with syrup, nuts or fruit.

clue.text: Copy section of newspaper

indicators.note: a section is a slice taken from within the word that follows

blocks.note: the letters sit near the end of newspaper

explanation.surface: Instruction to duplicate part of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or mimic them, i.e. to copy.

clue.text: Beg head of retail to split salary

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
something that splits another goes into its middle, dividing it in two

explanation.surface: Pleading with the boss of a shop to share out the wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the sense of imploring or entreating someone is a synonym of beg.

clue.text: Filthy spectacle after yob beheaded

indicators.note: to behead is to cut off the top, so the first letter is removed
after places the word before it second, behind the word that follows it in the clue

blocks.note: a yob is a British word for a loutish young man
a scene is a public display, a spectacle

explanation.surface: A disgusting sight follows the execution of a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the spectacle second, behind the shortened yob.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensively indecent, and filthy is a common synonym in that sense.
